newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI, Motorola to bid in Brazil cellular auction.
newsitem.headline: DDI, Motorola to bid in Brazil cellular auction.

text.p: Japan's second biggest phone operator, DDI Corp, said on Thursday that it plans, together with Motorola Inc, to bid in the Brazilian auction of cellular "Band-B" concessions planned for April 7.
"We haven't been informed of the schedule yet, but if the auction is as planned on April 7, we will definitely bid," a DDI spokesman said.
The consortium will include two local interests, communications equipment maker Inepar SA Industria e Construcoes and petrochemical maker Cia Suzano de Papel e Celulose, the spokesman said.
Several other local companies may also join the consortium, he said.
This would become DDI's first overseas project if the group wins the order.
Brazil's Communications Ministry, in its bid invitation, listed 10 concessions, two of which will be announced first.
Operators must prove they are capable of serving 1.8 million customers in each of the largest two concessions.
The group plans to bid for several concessions, such as the lucrative Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais states, the DDI spokesman said.
Brazil has a population of about 160 million but only about nine lines per 100 people, according to Latin Trade magazine.
Besides the DDI/Motorola group, more than a dozen consortiums, including among them BellSouth Corp and AT & T Corp, are expected to put in bids at the auction.
